summary: Follow a diagram from the browser to the Go API, then see how Stripe events reach a worker through MongoDB and Amazon SQS.
scope: Follow Thoth’s browser editor, Go API and Stripe billing pipeline. Cloud storage and hosted sharing require an eligible account. Check View plans in Thoth for current availability. The arrows show how requests and jobs move through the system.
author: Thoth

componentNotes.client: The Next.js editor saves on the device and can keep working when the API is unavailable. The browser sends Firebase ID tokens on authenticated API requests.
componentNotes.local: The browser persists the editable workspace in localStorage. JSON export lets the user keep a portable copy.
componentNotes.api: One Go process serves the API. It verifies identity, checks tenant membership and paid entitlements, and composes the storage, cache, queue and payment adapters.
componentNotes.mongo: Atlas stores application records and tenant-scoped workspaces. MongoDB transactions enforce quotas, idempotency and subscription updates.
componentNotes.redis: Redis supplies a disposable cache. The API checks its connectivity through health. Identity and paid access are resolved from the services that verify them.
componentNotes.posthog: The browser sends selected anonymous events, including native pageviews. Diagram content and URL query parameters stay out of the event payload.
componentNotes.sentry: The Go API reports sanitized errors and sampled request traces. Reports use route templates and omit request bodies and credentials.
componentNotes.firebase: Firebase supplies Google and passwordless email sign-in. The Go API verifies the token and current verified identity before resolving access.
componentNotes.checkout: Stripe hosts the payment form. The server chooses the price and seat count. Returning from Checkout cannot grant a subscription.
componentNotes.inbox: The verified Stripe event ID and publication intent are committed together in MongoDB before acknowledgement. The inbox gives the worker a durable recovery source.
componentNotes.queue: Amazon SQS Standard delivers jobs at least once. The message carries an event ID. A failed attempt can be retried and repeated failures reach the dead-letter queue.
componentNotes.worker: The Go API runs the worker when billing is enabled. It reads Stripe's current state, applies a fenced MongoDB transaction and acknowledges completed work after the commit.
